This is the documented knife-edge class, never the gate.

verdict.ds41_this_operating_point: NO-GO. Exit measured: hit + tok/s at 1/2/4 cards vs baselines. Hit is FLAT (the cache was never the limiter at this operating point); the rate is NEGATIVE at every sharding (-9.4% t2, -25..-27.5% t4/t4e) and the attribution boot EXONERATES the host-sum round trip (-3.3%), localizing the cost to the per-layer fan-out itself: run() is synchronous by design, so a sharded decode pays N serialized tier submissions + N launch groups per layer instead of one.
verdict.what_would_change_it: an engine where the shard runs OVERLAP (per-shard streams + one join per layer, and a device-side fan-in) - and even then the ceiling is the miss headroom: +0.2 pt hit at best on this profile. Not worth the plumbing for DS4.1.
verdict.live_axis: the CACHE-STARVED engine: GLM-5.3 Maya-L decode runs hit 12.4%, cpu pool 75.9% = 275-285 ms/token of its 306-337 ms/token wall (logs/p5.4c-g_*-20261027-180516.log, p5.4-g_ctl-20261026-214909.log). There the tier IS the wall and it is byte-bound CPU-pool compute: four shards = four CPU pools + four byte-supply pipes + 4x VRAM/arena on the SAME hot set distribution. That port (mirror the fan-out + n_ent into tools/ds4/ds4_moe.hpp/.cpp and glm_generate.cpp) is NEW TASK #42; the host algebra gate pattern (test_ds41_moe --shards) ports with it.

lessons: shard 0 must take its arena slice too: mc carried the full --arena-gib and shard 1 added arena/N -> 90 GiB pinned vs the 84 GiB scope (fixed 4de1f021; the MemAvailable gate measures the TOTAL arena, the scope catches the mistake)
never WARM=0 after a vLLM (re)start: the first boot is a 2.4x page-cache artifact and it poisons the SAME-ROUND pairing, which is the whole point of interleaving
engine counters behaved: identical lookup totals across arms made the residency-confound check a one-line grep
prompt tok/s on a 16-token prompt is meaningless (load-dominated); long-prompt scaling stays with P5.5-style runners
